review_note: Granted on native Poisson animal(pedigree) fits only. (1) The oracle is independent of the package. A is built by a hand-written Henderson tabular method (helper-sb26-oracle.R, no drmTMB internals) and checked against drmTMB:::drm_pedigree_additive_relationship at 1e-12 on an inbred pedigree (diag(A) up to 1.25). The marginal is a dense base-R Laplace evaluated at the fitted parameters. logLik agreement was 2.9e-11 and 2.3e-12 in my Totoro rerun (cores 174-179), against a tolerance of 1e-4. (2) Emulated-bug gaps from my rerun, which printed each gap, are far beyond that tolerance. Slope-only fit: cov2cor(A) 0.48, reversed SD vector 227, flipped v-slope sign 442, pedigree order read as factor order 20.8. Intercept-plus-slope fit: swapped selectors 143, reversed SDs 98, cov2cor(A) 0.57, A in the wrong order 52.7. The smallest gaps (0.48 and 0.57) are over 4,000 times the tolerance. The SD curves are non-trivial (sd of log SD 0.48 and 1.06). (3) Fitted rows: animal_numeric_slope is fitted twice, as slope-only animal(0 + x | id) with sd ~ v, and as the slope member of the unlabelled animal(1 + x | id), which is two independent fields with one SD formula each (sd ~ w on the intercept, sd ~ v on x). The animal_intercept row is supported only as the intercept member of that two-field fit, because no intercept-only animal(1 | id) fit exists, so the 'single additive-genetic field' wording is met only per coefficient. (4) Manifest: all 7 sha256 values match current files; the test is byte-identical to the ledger hash. The console log shows 22 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skips, and 3 blocks. It also reports 0 live Julia tests, which is correct for this native id. Does NOT establish: that a lone intercept-only animal(1 | id) pedigree fit was tested; the animal_correlated_block (shared-rho) rows, since the two fields are independent; Ainv_precision or A_covariance animal rows (only pedigree input); other families or links; Julia parity; interval calibration, coverage, recovery or estimator accuracy; any broad parity claim.
